question: Why does gradient descent need a learning rate?
reference_answer: The learning rate sets how big each update step is. Too small makes learning slow; too large can overshoot the minimum.
rubric: Learning rate is the size of each step | Used when updating the weights | Too small: learning is slow | Too large: overshoots the minimum
student_answer: It controls how big each step is when we update the weights.

question: What is overfitting?
reference_answer: Overfitting is when a model learns the training data too closely, including noise, so it performs badly on new data.
rubric: Model fits training data too closely | Performs badly on new data
student_answer: The model memorizes the training set and then fails on data it has not seen.
